steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (a field name is an interface others call), so I'm stopping before editing.

The consequence: `routes/users.js:6` emits `userId` in the `GET /users` response body. Renaming it to `user_id` is a breaking change for every consumer that reads that field. `README.md` names them explicitly — the web app, the iOS app 3.2+, and the nightly partner export — and states that response field names are part of the contract and that changes go through a versioned endpoint. The iOS clients in particular can't be updated in lockstep with the server.

So "just the field name" is exactly the part that breaks: `orders` already uses `user_id`, so the inconsistency is real, but the fix as stated ships a contract break to shipped mobile builds and a partner job.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README's stated policy: keep /users emitting userId, and expose the snake_case shape on a new versioned endpoint (e.g. /v2/users). No break for the web app, iOS 3.2+, or the partner export. Largest change.

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Add user_id alongside userId in the existing /users response, so new consumers can migrate and old ones keep working. Deprecate userId later. Small change, no break, but the response carries a duplicate field for a while.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Do exactly what was asked: change userId to user_id in routes/users.js. One-line change. Breaks the web app, shipped iOS 3.2+ builds, and the nightly partner export until each is updated.
